title: Touring with the reformed Original Dixieland Band
summary: After Nick's, Sharkey joins the band after La Rocca left; they tour but quarrel as a cooperative with no leader.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I'm sorry, most of all I missed Shields, the only chance I ever had to hear him. Then they got that Dixieland band together and traveled around the country and I just missed them in Memphis and I missed them down here about 1937. Yeah, I played with them. Yeah, you made some records then when La Rocca left.
La Rocca left and came back home and I was finished at Nix and they asked me would I join them and I joined them. Did you travel with them?

We went to... Oh, I wasn't sure if you traveled with them. Yes, we went to Oklahoma, Houston, Texas, Shreveport. Well, I forgot that you traveled, yeah, on that tour. I traveled with them for quite a while and I hate... there's another thing that I don't like to say, but they couldn't get along.
Yeah, well, I mean La Rocca has told that story too, he always complained. Yeah, but... Everybody blamed everybody else, so... That's right.

You see, when we'd get on a bandstand and when it come time to play a number, well, one would say, let's play this and everyone would say, oh, let's play this, let's play that. And we'd be organ five, ten minutes before we'd get to play one tune. So I'd say, oh, let's play this and I'd just go off with it. Yeah, that's the way you do. So I got tired of that. I said, I'm going home.
Yeah. Well, Eddie Edwards is dead now too, I guess. He was the manager, I guess, in a way, and tried to run it, and then La Rocca was the leader, or so it was a...
Well, it was a co-op thing, and everybody had the same say-so, and that is where the trouble was.
The trumpet ought to be the leader, though, in a New Orleans band. That's right. It's a tradition to have the leader. Right.

They should have a man to do all the business, and after he'd do that business, then all get together and say, now, this is what's going to happen. We'll play here so and so, so and so. See? After all, they organized that band to make money, which they did make a lot of money, but
